equity_bridge.item: Retained 19.85% stake in The Magnum Ice Cream Company (TMICC) at fair value
equity_bridge.note: H1 2026 report, financial assets note (d): FVOCI equity investment EUR1,852m at 30 June 2026 (31 Dec 2025: 1,655). Outside net debt; management intends to sell down over time.

equity_bridge.item: Joint ventures, associates and other non-current investments at 10x FY2025 share of profit/income
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 cash flow statement: share of net profit of JVs/associates and other income from non-current investments EUR228m (2024: 263; 2023: 206), mainly Pepsi Lipton. This income is outside EBIT and so outside the flows; 10x post-tax is half the 20x core terminal cap. Covers the EUR595m of other FVOCI equity investments too, so those are not added separately.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance: multi-year USG 4-6% (FY2026 toward the top, H1 2026 USG 4.8%) less ~1pp structural EM-currency translation drag into EUR; year 1 set at 2.0% for the guided ~3% FY2026 FX headwind net of H1 2026 reported turnover +0.5% and M&A (Gruns, Wild). Equity CAGR is not usable as a growth anchor: book equity was reduced by the Ice Cream demerger distribution and a decade of buybacks.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity, revenue and EPS CAGRs all span the Dec 2025 Ice Cream demerger and the 8-for-9 consolidation: FY2022 and earlier are consolidated (incl. ~EUR8bn Ice Cream turnover), FY2023 onward are restated continuing. The 3-yr figures are therefore basis breaks, not trends. Like-for-like: continuing revenue FY2023 51,680 -> FY2025 50,503 (-1.1%/yr, FX-driven; USG was +4.2% and +3.6%); consolidated as-originally-reported revenue FY2015 53,272 -> FY2024 60,761 (+1.5%/yr).
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - 0 interest): FY2020 7,929 (consolidated, COVID working-capital windfall year), FY2022 5,396, FY2025 6,206 (continuing). SBC is 0.4-0.6% of revenue throughout, so SBC-adjusted and reported CAGRs are within 0.2pp; SBC is not absorbing growth here. Reported EUR revenue growth has lagged underlying sales growth by ~2-3pp/yr over the decade (FX translation and disposals), which is why the base nominal EUR growth path sits ~1pp under the USG guidance range.

scenario_narratives.base: Unilever post-demerger is a four-segment staples compounder: underlying sales growth in the 4-6% range (FY2026 at the top on the best volume growth since 2010), translated into ~3.5% nominal EUR growth after the structural emerging-market currency drag that has cost 2-3pp/yr for a decade. Underlying operating margin improves modestly from 20.0% toward ~21% by the mid-2030s as Power Brands (78% of turnover) and Prestige Beauty & Wellbeing (Dermalogica, Paula's Choice, Nutrafol, Liquid I.V., Gruns) raise mix, while restructuring stays a recurring ~1% of turnover rather than a one-off. The axes that decide this case are (1) whether the H1 2026 volume acceleration persists once H2 growth becomes price-led, (2) whether EM price resets (Thailand) remain contained, and (3) EUR translation. Terminal value is bound by the 20x owner-FCF cap (Gordon at 7%/2.5% would be 22.8x).
scenario_narratives.bull: The Growth Action Plan works: USG holds at ~6% with EM volume (India via Hindustan Unilever, Turkey, Vietnam, Indonesia) and US premiumisation both delivering, FX turns neutral, and the simplified portfolio converts productivity into ~22% underlying operating margins by the early 2030s, closing part of the gap to P&G. The TMICC sell-down and EUR6bn 2026-29 buyback programme recycle capital without adding leverage. Tax plus minority leakage eases to 32.5% as the underlying ETR settles at the guided 26%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The volume recovery proves to be price investment, not demand: resets spread across cash-strained Asian markets, private label keeps taking Home Care and Foods share in Europe and the US, and USG slips back to the 3-3.5% of FY2025 while EM currencies keep depreciating against the EUR, leaving 1.5-2% nominal growth. Margins give back the demerger uplift (UOM ~19%) as marketing is reinvested and restructuring recurs; a third CEO change in a decade and renewed activist pressure follow. No solvency element: net debt/UEBITDA stays ~2.5x and the dividend is covered, so the bear case is a de-rating to a 16x terminal multiple, not a distress path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Unilever as a mature, net-indebted staples compounder on continuing-operations owner FCF: SBC expensed, share count flat, leases in net debt, minority leakage in the flows, non-operating assets (TMICC stake, JVs) added back once because their income is outside the flows. The valuation is terminal-dominated and capped at 20x owner FCF; the 7% EUR WACC carries the EM translation risk once. The honest finding is that the NYSE price sits near the base case: the market is paying for the Growth Action Plan delivering roughly what management guides, with no margin of safety against the bear path.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value is ~60%+ of EV and bound by the 20x cap; a 2x change in the cap moves value ~8-10%.
Structural EM-currency translation drag (2-3pp/yr historically) is modelled at ~1pp; if the decade repeats, the base case overstates nominal EUR growth.

Restructuring is modelled as a permanent ~1% of turnover; if management's 'one-off' framing is right, value is understated by ~EUR2-3/share, if the EUR800m programme is followed by another, as every prior programme was, the base is right.
NCI leakage is held at 8.55% of profit; Hindustan Unilever grows faster than the group and its minority is 38%, so leakage drifts up over time.
Pension surplus (EUR3.7bn) and the 20x-plus multiple the market assigns to HUL are both excluded; the model is conservative on both.
FX: fx_rate 1.1257 EUR->USD is dated 2026-10-02; refresh_price.py moves the price but not the rate.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for UL (NYSE, USD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 54.75-74.98. Parity: UNA.AS (EUR) and ULVR.L (GBp) same-day closes, EURUSD=X for the rate.
data_sources.financials: UL_Metrics.csv (continuing-operations basis from FY2023; financial-parser adjudication), UL_Annual_FY2025.txt (20-F: non-underlying items table, FCF reconciliation, cash flow statement, TMICC fair value 1,672 at demerger), UL_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (net debt reconciliation, diluted shares 2,183m, TMICC stake 1,852, pension surplus 3.7bn, restructuring guidance ~1.0% of turnover, UETR ~26%, net finance cost <3% of net debt).
data_sources.qualitative: UL_Analysis.json (Growth Action Plan 2030, Power Brands, EM price resets, guidance raised at H1 2026 to the top of the 4-6% USG range).

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 20-F consolidated cash flow statement, 'Non-cash charge for share-based compensation' 255 (2024: 292; 2023: 192), continuing operations. EquityAwardTaxes 0: Unilever settles share plans from treasury shares (TreasuryPurchasesForSharePlans ~EUR200-270m/yr historically), no net-share-settlement tax line.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate is EUR->USD (reporting -> quote, the dcf_engine convention): EURUSD=X 1.1257 on Yahoo Finance at 2026-10-02T21:29Z. Parity check against the Euronext Amsterdam ordinary line: UNA.AS EUR 52.84 x 1.1257 = USD 59.48 vs NYSE UL USD 59.70 at the 2026-10-02 close, a 0.4% tie that confirms the direction, the rate and that one NYSE UL share = one ordinary share (no ADS ratio). ULVR.L 4,483.5 GBp cross-checks at the same time. Note scripts/sanity_check.py documents the opposite (quote->reporting) convention for this field; see sanity_check_note if it trips.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T20:00:02Z regular close (Friday; valuation written Saturday 2026-10-04, no after-hours print)
inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted average number of shares H1 2026, 2,183m (H1 2026 report, EPS note), post the 8-for-9 consolidation of 9 Dec 2025 and the EUR1.5bn H1 2026 buyback (30.7m shares). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows; buybacks (EUR1.5bn/yr, EUR6bn guided 2026-29) are the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and are value-neutral here.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Company-defined net debt EUR25,961m at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 report net debt reconciliation): total financial liabilities 32,110 (INCLUDING lease liabilities ~EUR1.3bn) less cash 4,726, less other current financial assets 1,322, less liability-related derivatives 101, plus overdrafts 55. Up from 23,076 at FY2025 on dividends, the buyback and the Gruns/Wild/Nutrafol acquisitions; management guides ND/UEBITDA ~2x at FY2026.
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR-built rate. Bottom-up: 10y Bund ~2.7%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~0.6 -> cost of equity ~6.0%; after-tax cost of debt ~2.5% (net finance cost guided <3% of net debt); D/(D+E) ~18% -> ~5.4%. House uses 7.0%: a ~1.5pp premium for the fact that more than half of turnover is earned in emerging-market currencies and translated into EUR, which a Bund-based rate does not carry. That is the only place EM risk is charged in the discount rate; the scenario flows carry execution and pricing risk, and WACC is identical across scenarios (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Lease liabilities (EUR1,326m at FY2025) stay inside the company-defined net debt; lease principal (EUR301m FY2025) is NOT deducted from the flows; ongoing lease-asset renewal is charged through the capex line: capex_pct 3.6% = 2.9% net cash capex (FY2025 1,465/50,503) + 0.7% lease additions (FY2025 lease-liability additions 341/50,503). D&A 2.6% (FY2025 1,310 ex impairment) includes right-of-use depreciation, consistent with (A).
inputs.nci_treatment: Charged ONCE, in the flows: cash_tax_rate_path is a combined tax-plus-leakage rate, 1 - (1 - 27% unlevered cash tax on EBIT) x (1 - 8.55% NCI share of continuing net profit, FY2025 531/6,213) = 33.2%, set 34.0% in FY2026 (H1 2026 cash tax elevated), 33.5% FY2027, 33.0% thereafter. NCI book value (EUR2,113m) is therefore NOT deducted in the bridge; the largest minority (38% of Hindustan Unilever) is valued on the same flow basis as the rest of the group.
inputs.ebitda_basis: adj_ebitda is pre-SBC, post-restructuring, post-IFRS-16. FY2025 continuing actual = (statutory operating profit 9,037 + D&A 1,353 + SBC 255)/50,503 = 21.1%; underlying EBITDA (UEBITDA 11,394) was 22.6% before EUR1,047m of non-underlying items (restructuring 599, acquisition/disposal 288, other 160). Forward paths assume restructuring continues at ~1.0% of turnover (FY2026 guidance) plus ~0.3% acquisition costs rather than treating them as one-offs; they have recurred every year for a decade.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US consumer' + owner-fcf-adaptations: currency, leases, NCI, matching-asset rule). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. BASIS: all FY0 anchors are CONTINUING OPERATIONS after the 6 Dec 2025 demerger of Ice Cream into The Magnum Ice Cream Company (TMICC): the FY2025 20-F cash flow statement is presented on a continuing basis (OCF 8,052, capex 1,591, SBC 255 are continuing lines; discontinued operating cash flow 298 is excluded), and the income statement comparatives FY2023/FY2024 are re-presented. last_fcf = 6,461 reported (continuing OCF 8,052 - capex 1,591; Unilever's own FCF of 5,921 additionally deducts net interest 666 and is a levered figure) - SBC 255 - interest income 0 = 6,206. Interest income (398) is NOT stripped because the company is a net borrower (ND/UEBITDA 2.3x), so there is no cash pile being double counted; finance income is simply outside the EBIT-based component build. MATCHING-ASSET RULE: share of JV/associate profit and income from non-current investments (EUR228m FY2025, mainly the Pepsi Lipton JV) sits outside operating profit and so outside the flows; those assets are added in equity_bridge (TMICC stake at fair value, JV/associates at 10x). The EUR3.7bn IAS 19 pension surplus is deliberately NOT added: pension income is outside the flows but the surplus is not accessible without buyout cost and tax; it is ~EUR1.7/share of unmodelled upside. HORIZON 10 years FY2026-FY2035 (margin still drifting up through year 5). WC capture is positive and small (5%) because Unilever runs negative working capital (payables > receivables + inventory); growth generates cash. Historical growth is a mixed basis (consolidated incl. Ice Cream through FY2022, restated continuing from FY2023), see historical_growth.notes.

bear.growth_rationale: USG slips to 3-3.5% (the FY2025 3.6% outcome, below the 4% floor of the range) as EM price resets spread beyond Thailand and private label takes share in Home Care/Foods; EM currency drag of 1.5pp leaves 1.5-2% nominal EUR growth, roughly the decade's as-reported 1.5% CAGR.
bear.margin_rationale: adj EBITDA settles at 21.0% (UOM ~19.0%, below the 19.5% GAP floor): price resets and reinvestment in brand and marketing absorb productivity savings, and restructuring never falls below 1% of turnover. Tax+leakage 34.5% (Pillar Two and faster-growing HUL raising the minority share). Terminal cap 16x for an ex-growth staple.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +2.0% reported EUR: USG ~5-6% (top of range, H1 4.8%) less ~3% FX headwind, plus Gruns/Wild. FY2027-30 3.5%: USG ~4.5% less ~1pp EM-currency drag. Fades to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: 22.0% in FY2026 = UOM ~20.2% (modest improvement on 20.0%, H1 2026 20.3%) less 1.3% non-underlying (restructuring 1.0% guided + acquisition costs) plus D&A 2.6% plus SBC 0.5%; H1 2026 statutory operating margin 19.1% + D&A + SBC ties to ~22.1%. Mature 23.0% = UOM ~20.9%, +90bps over a decade from Power Brands mix, premium Beauty & Wellbeing and productivity: the Growth Action Plan ambition, not P&G parity.

bull.growth_rationale: USG sustained at the 6% top of range on EM volume (India, Turkey, Vietnam) and US premium beauty/wellness, with FX neutral to mildly positive; 5% nominal EUR FY2027-29.
bull.margin_rationale: UOM reaches ~22.4% by FY2035 (adj EBITDA 24.5% - SBC 0.5% - D&A 2.6% + restructuring 1.0%): Power Brands mix, restructuring fading toward 0.5-0.7% and the EUR800m productivity programme fully delivered. Lower tax+leakage (32.5%) as underlying ETR settles at the guided ~26%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (second CEO in three years executing a new growth plan on a freshly demerged base) and the FY2025 USG of 3.6% already sat below the 4% floor of the guided range, so the bear path is the recent past, not a tail. Bull cut to 25%: it needs three independent things to go right (sustained EM volume, benign EUR translation, and margin convergence toward P&G) against a decade in which reported EUR revenue compounded at 1.5%. No going-concern element, so bear is not pushed higher.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
